text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima says Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank's first option for Bank Austria shares is unrelated to Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt earlier this year. He rejects conservative Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner's demand to revoke the sale.
- The European Commission plans to halve its regional subsidies to Austria, as it says most of the country does not need it anymore.
- Creditanstalt and insurer EA-Generali are slowly moving apart following Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt.

- Social Democrat Josef Cap says conditions for Austria joining NATO must be reviewed before any decisions can be made. He criticised his party's chief whip Peter Kostelka for strictly refusing NATO membership.
- Austria's unemployment rate remained steady at 4.4 percent in May compared to the month before.

- The Oesterreichische Volksbanken AG sees Germany's Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank as the future central bank in the co-operative banking sector when European economic and monetary union is introduced.
DIE PRESSE
- Chancellor Klima says he did not know of Westdeutsche Landesbank's first option on further Bank Austria shares of the City of Vienna. A political scandal is brewing over the affair.
- Conservative vice-party leader Elisabeth Zanon says her party will reduce pressure in the debate around Austria's possible future membership in NATO.

- A draft telecommunications law has not yet passed the council of ministers as conservatives are demanding a more thorough examination of a new law that should abolish Post & Telekom Austria's monopoly.
- U.S. telecommunications group SBC plans to bid for Austria's third mobile phone licence after not having become the strategic partner of Post & Telekom Austria's mobile phone comapny Mobilkom.
- Austria's Volksbanken feels discriminated against by Austria's tax laws as it paid more taxes than Bank Austria, Creditanstalt, Bawag and Die Erste savings bank together.
- Postal savings bank PSK will be able to sell private loans soon after an eight-year-break.
- Research institute IHS expects Austria's unemployment to go go down by 1999.
- Real estate financer Immofinanz plans to expand more.
- Public backing for Europe's single currency euro has increased slightly, but disapproval is still high.
KURIER
- Conservatives want to privatise Bank Austria with "full force". Farnleitner is still threatening to annul the bank's takeover of Creditanstalt.
- Social Democrat General Secretary Andreas Rudas expects no tax raises to be necessary for the 1998 budget.
- Austrian Airlines wants to take over the stake of industrialist Gernot Langes-Swarovski in Tyrolean Airways, of which it is the majority shareholder.

- EA-Generali is searching for a partner as it has just cancelled its partnership with Creditanstalt. Now it is fighting with insurance holding BARC over the sale of contracts in Die Erste savings banks.
- Milk producer NOeM will increase its capital by 400 million schillings as all reserves were used up by the company's losses.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Austrian states demand the road-pricing system be introduced on the country's motorways before road financing company Asfinag's debt can be excluded from the federal budget.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger plans to start selling the government's 18-percent stake in Bank Austria this year.
